our_argument_summary: Self-Contradicted. K1 (23.9345 h, sidereal-day-derived) is trivial luni-solar diurnal arithmetic. Dome's local moon at 2,534 km (d/R≈0.13) concentrates declination forcing in a localized cone beneath the sub-lunar point, not the global latitude-dependent diurnal inequality observed. Also post-hoc: K1 is textbook physics, pred=obs=23.9345h to four decimals — a constant-equals-constant comparison sourced from IERS catalogue (raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 218).

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: K1 is the standard luni-solar diurnal harmonic constituent in classical tidal theory (Doodson 1921 onwards). Period derivation: K1 ≈ T_sidereal_day = 23.9345 h. The dome model adopts the catalogue period unchanged — no dome-geometry derivation produces this number.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: K1 = 23.9345 h has been the catalogued luni-solar diurnal period since Doodson's 1921 harmonic expansion (DOI 10.1098/rspa.1921.0088). The dome's claimed 'prediction' is a transcription of the IERS-published value by the dome author's own admission (dashboard 'Source: IERS published' label).
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: No dome-geometry derivation exists for K1 = 23.9345 h. The number is adopted directly from the IERS catalogue (per dome's own dashboard label). The dome geometry — moon at 2,534 km, d/R ≈ 0.13 — would in fact predict the WRONG spatial distribution for K1's amplitude (localized declination spike rather than smooth latitude-dependent global modulation), which is the self-contradiction this WIN flags.

stronger_arguments.description: The 0.01% tolerance is itself a kill-shot worth surfacing. Tidal period determination via harmonic decomposition cannot reach 0.01% precision in either prediction OR observation — both numbers are catalogue-derived. A 0.01% tolerance whose only physical meaning is 'pred-must-equal-obs-to-four-decimals' is a constant-equals-constant lookup masquerading as a measurement comparison. This logic is already in WIN-046's verdict text but not WIN-049's; parallelising the posture imports this argument for free.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model is correct that K1 = 23.9345 h is the catalogued luni-solar diurnal period (this is verifiable against IERS conventions and Doodson 1921; see code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence in this review). It is also true that any model with a ~24-hour rotation and a moon with non-zero declination will produce a K1 spectral peak — the existence of K1 isn't dome-specific, and the dome's monitoring detects this correctly (raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 216-218 records pred=obs=23.9345). What's unusual is the dome author's own forthrightness: the dashboard label 'Source: IERS published' is itself a candid statement that this isn't a live measurement.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Having a correct number that anyone can read from a published catalogue isn't a prediction — under the dome author's own framing (per current detail_verdict_text citing his predictions page definition) a prediction is 'derived from the model, registered with a timestamp, and subsequently confirmed by independent data.' Pred=obs=23.9345 with both sides labeled 'Source: IERS published' fails each clause. Beyond the post-hoc problem, the dome's geometric prediction for K1's spatial distribution (localized declination spike from the d/R≈0.13 moon, see code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence) contradicts the observed smooth latitude-dependent diurnal inequality — so the period match would still be vacuous even if it WERE prospective: the period is a trivial consequence of having a rotating moon, and the dome fails on the harder pattern test.

deeper_analysis: The interesting story isn't WIN-049 itself — that's a clean Self-Contradicted call backed by quantitative verification (see quantitative_verification, all checks passed). The interesting story is the c4→c5 trace of the cross-WIN cluster (WIN-045/046/049). The c4 review proposed two paths: (a) harden all three with citations [preferred], (b) propagate the hedge from WIN-049 to WIN-045/046 [fallback]. Decider chose (a) for two of three, leaving (b) implicit on the third. ISS-1798/1812 fix_details described this as 'propagated the hedge' but actually delivered the opposite (hardening). This is the exact pattern PROP-047 was written for — closure-ledger descriptions that don't match actual data — and it shows up in carry-over hygiene: the c4 hole text quoted 'are hardcoded static constants in monitor.py' which is correctly absent from current data, BUT the underlying posture issue persists in mirror form. The phrase-presence re-grep (Step 5a) correctly identifies the c4 hole's verbatim claim as stale; the c5 hole rewrites the concern in current terms. This is what good carry-over hygiene looks like: don't re-assert the exact c4 grievance, do re-assert the structural concern using current evidence.

quantitative_verification.computations: K1 = 23.9345 h vs sidereal day 23.9344696 h: difference 0.00003 h (0.0001%) — within four-decimal precision. d/R = 2534/20015 = 0.1266 ≈ 0.13. Tidal force falloff using (1/r^3) with r = sqrt(h^2 + offset^2): at 5,000 km offset, r=5605.4 km, ratio (2534/5605.4)^3 = 0.0924 = 9.24% ≈ 9%. At 10,008 km offset (equator from sub-lunar point on AE projection), r=10324 km, ratio (2534/10324)^3 = 0.01481 = 1.48%. K1 equilibrium amplitude ~16.7 cm at equator; observed varies regionally 10-50 cm; '~14 cm at open ocean' falls in the lower regional range — hedge holds. All quantitative claims in WIN-049 detail_evidence verify.
